figures.caption: Integral nonlinearity of the \(R\)--\(2R\) ladder driven from an ideal \SI{2.5}{\volt} reference. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, model section \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, seed 12345, low-discrepancy sampling, \SI{25}{\celsius}, all 4096 codes. The dashed rule is the \(1\,\mathrm{LSB}\) limit entered on the test; 42 of 200 samples fall inside it and the worst reaches \(3.453\,\mathrm{LSB}\). The distribution is right-skewed (Fisher skew \(+0.74\)), so Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-ideal} quotes the median and percentiles rather than mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\). LSB size, full scale and gain error are fixed to a part in \(10^{6}\) on this bench (Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-scale}), so the whole of this spread is resistor mismatch in the ladder and none of it is the reference.

Worst negative differential nonlinearity, same bench, samples and conditions as Figure~\ref{fig:dacr2r12-mc-inl}. The dashed rule at \(-1\,\mathrm{LSB}\) is the monotonicity limit entered on the test: 80 of 200 samples clear it, so \SI{40}{\percent} of channels are monotonic and \(0.40^4 = \SI{2.6}{\percent}\) of four-channel chips are monotonic on all four. The distribution is left-skewed (skew \(-1.11\)) with a tail to \(-6.608\,\mathrm{LSB}\), so the median \(-1.318\,\mathrm{LSB}\) and the percentiles of Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-ideal} describe it and mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) does not.

The quarter-LSB budget of \SI{133}{\micro\volt} entered on the test sits about 200 times below the data, so it is annotated at the left axis edge rather than drawn and the distribution is not compressed into a single bar; the closest sample misses it by a factor of 144. Meeting it needs the supply's output impedance down by a factor of 193, to about \SI{5}{\ohm}, against \SI{894}{\ohm} small-signal (Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-psu-zout}) and \SI{1133}{\ohm} as a \SI{0}{\micro\ampere} to \SI{100}{\micro\ampere} chord (Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-psu-load}).

Output resistance of the DAC supply block, taken as the chord \(\Delta V/\Delta I\) over a \SI{0}{\micro\ampere} to \SI{100}{\micro\ampere} load sweep on \texttt{VddDac}. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{27}{\celsius}. The \SI{3}{\ohm} limit entered on the test is two orders of magnitude below the data and is annotated at the left axis edge rather than drawn; no sample meets it. This is not a second defect: the reference movement of Figure~\ref{fig:dacr2r12-mc-vddacpp} is this impedance multiplied by the ladder's own code-dependent reference current.

tables.caption: Monte Carlo static linearity of the \(R\)--\(2R\) ladder on an ideal \SI{2.5}{\volt} reference. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, model section \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, seed 12345, low-discrepancy sampling, \SI{25}{\celsius}, all 4096 codes, \texttt{reltol}~\num{1e-6}; the yield columns are per cent of samples and of four independent channels. The ladder fails on its own: 42 of 200 samples hold INL below \(1\,\mathrm{LSB}\), 80 of 200 are monotonic, and both together on 34 of 200 --- \SI{17.0}{\percent} of channels and \SI{0.08}{\percent} of four-channel chips. Only the three worst-case rows carry limits entered on the test; \texttt{inl\_max}, \texttt{inl\_min} and \texttt{dnl\_max} were not graded and their spec, yield and worst-case cells are therefore empty. Worst-magnitude INL is the negative extreme on all 200 samples, so the first and third rows are one measurement with opposite sign, while \texttt{inl\_max} is the independent positive extreme. All three graded rows are skewed (Figures~\ref{fig:dacr2r12-mc-inl} and~\ref{fig:dacr2r12-mc-dnl}), so the median and percentiles are quoted and mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) is not.

Monte Carlo scale factors, same bench and samples as Table~ef{tab:dacr2r12-mc-ideal}. 	extbf{Process and mismatch}, 	exttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{25}{\celsius}. On an ideal reference these four are set by the rail and by the ladder's attenuation ratio, not by matching: LSB size spreads \SI{0.5}{
ano\volt} on \SI{610.3}{\micro\volt}, full scale \SI{1.8}{\micro\volt} on \SI{2.5}{\volt}, and gain error 
um{0.50}~ppm on 
um{-76.91}~ppm. All of the linearity spread of Table~ef{tab:dacr2r12-mc-ideal} is therefore ladder mismatch and none of it is a gain or offset term. No limit was entered on any of these outputs, so the spec, yield and worst-case columns are omitted rather than left blank; mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) is not quoted either, because at a part in \(10^{6}\) the distribution shapes are solver residue and not device statistics.

Monte Carlo linearity with the ladder referenced to \texttt{VddDac} from the on-chip supply block: ratiometric rows first, raw rows below. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{25}{\celsius}, all 4096 codes, no external load on \texttt{VddDac}; yields are per cent of samples and of four channels. The ratiometric rows normalise each code to the reference at that code and so measure the ladder alone; they reproduce Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-ideal} sample for sample, at \(r = 1.000\) on both INL and DNL, and their yields are \SI{20.5}{\percent} and \SI{40.0}{\percent} against \SI{21.0}{\percent} and \SI{40.0}{\percent} there. The raw rows include the reference and are 24 and 6 times worse; the run's own \texttt{inl\_from\_ref}, which is the INL predicted from the reference error alone, averages \num{36.770}\,LSB against the raw \num{36.776}\,LSB, so the reference accounts for essentially all of the difference and no second matching mechanism is needed to explain it. Raw \texttt{inl\_lsb} carries no entered limit and its spec, yield and worst-case cells are empty; raw \texttt{dnl\_min} was graded and no sample meets it. The three ratiometric rows are skewed (\(+0.74\), \(-1.10\), \(+0.89\)), so the median and percentiles are quoted throughout.

Monte Carlo behaviour of the \texttt{VddDac} reference itself, same bench and samples as Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-wpsu}; only \texttt{vddac\_pp} carries an entered limit, so the other four rows have empty spec, yield and worst-case cells. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{25}{\celsius}; yields are per cent of samples and of four channels. Full scale is \SI{2.166}{\volt} and the LSB \SI{529.0}{\micro\volt} rather than \SI{2.5}{\volt} and \SI{610.3}{\micro\volt}, because the supply block delivers about \SI{2.15}{\volt}; the reference then moves \SI{25.8}{\milli\volt} peak to peak across the code sweep against the \SI{133}{\micro\volt} quarter-LSB budget, which no sample meets. The excursion is not monotonic in code: in an \(R\)--\(2R\) ladder the binary weighting comes from attenuation, so every \(2R\) branch switched to the reference draws a comparable current and the reference current follows the bit pattern rather than the code value --- a nodal solve of this topology gives \(I_\mathrm{ref} = 0\) at code 0, \(0.250\,V_\mathrm{ref}/R\) at 2048 and \(0.333\) at 4095, with a maximum of \(1.444\) at code 1365 (\texttt{0b010101010101}), which is exactly where \texttt{vddac\_min} lands on all 200 samples, and a one-parameter fit \(V = V_0 - R_\mathrm{out} I_\mathrm{ref}\) accounts for \SI{94}{\percent} of the excursion. All five distributions are near-symmetric (skew \(\leq 0.13\)), so mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) applies.

Monte Carlo load regulation of the DAC supply block. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{27}{\celsius}, \texttt{VddDac} loaded \SI{0}{\micro\ampere} to \SI{100}{\micro\ampere}, ADE default tolerances --- looser than the two DAC benches, which run \SI{25}{\celsius} and \texttt{reltol}~\num{1e-6}; yields are per cent of samples and of four channels. \texttt{VddDac} droops \SI{113.3}{\milli\volt} over that sweep, a chord output resistance of \SI{1132.8}{\ohm} against the \SI{3}{\ohm} limit entered on the test; no sample meets either graded limit, and the two reference-voltage rows were not graded. The last two rows are one measurement scaled by the load current, and both are near-symmetric (skew \(+0.29\)), so mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) applies. Together with the reference movement of Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-reference} and the small-signal impedance of Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-psu-zout} this is one defect measured three ways, not three problems.

Monte Carlo line regulation and quiescent power of the DAC supply block. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{27}{\celsius}, supply swept \SI{2.25}{\volt} to \SI{2.75}{\volt}, \texttt{VddDac} unloaded, ADE default tolerances; yields are per cent of samples and of four channels. \texttt{VddDac} follows the supply by \SI{78.8}{\milli\volt} over that \SI{0.5}{\volt} span, a rejection of only \SI{0.158}{\volt\per\volt}, against the \SI{5}{\milli\volt} limit entered on the test that no sample meets. Only \texttt{dvddac\_line} was graded; the other three rows have empty spec, yield and worst-case cells, the last two being the same measurement scaled by the \SI{2.5}{\volt} supply. All four are right-skewed (\(+0.58\), \(+0.58\), \(+0.45\), \(+0.45\)), so the median and percentiles are quoted and mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) is not.

Monte Carlo small-signal output impedance of the DAC supply block, AC swept \SI{1}{\hertz} to \SI{1}{\giga\hertz}. \textbf{Process and mismatch}, \texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}, 200 samples, \SI{27}{\celsius}, \texttt{VddDac} unloaded, ADE default tolerances; yields are per cent of samples and of four channels. The impedance is flat at \SI{894.3}{\ohm} to within \SI{0.4}{\ohm} from \SI{1}{\hertz} to \SI{100}{\kilo\hertz}, and this is the value that sets the reference movement of Table~\ref{tab:dacr2r12-mc-reference}, the ladder's code-dependent current being a DC excursion. \texttt{zout\_max} is the peak over the whole band and lands at \SI{98.9}{\mega\hertz}, loop peaking well above anything the ladder excites; it is the only graded row here and no sample meets its \SI{10}{\ohm} limit. \texttt{zout\_max} is strongly left-skewed (skew \(-1.82\)), so the median and percentiles are quoted; \texttt{zout\_lf} and the peak frequency carry no entered limit and their spec, yield and worst-case cells are empty.

_note: Monte Carlo companion for castalia/tb_anatop_pixel_dacR2R12 (the 12-bit R-2R
reference DAC and its supply block). Contributes fragments only: the master file
and the section order come from the corner config (block DacR2R12), whose `order`
names every fragment below. This config deliberately has no `order` of its own --
adding one would emit a second, competing section. Block is DacR2R12MC, distinct
from DacR2R12 / AmpAB / AmpABMC / TiaAmpAB / TiaAmpABMC / BiasGenCascWideSwing.
Logical test names are prefixed dac_mc_ because data/raw/<test>__mc.csv is a
namespace shared by every block rendering into one outdir.
SOURCE: .../tb_anatop_pixel_dacR2R12/maestro/results/maestro/Plan.2.Run.3
200 samples, seed=12345, sampling=lds, variations=all (PROCESS AND MISMATCH
together), donominal=no, numruns=20. Per-sample scalars are in
psf/<test>/monteCarlo/{mcdata,mcparam}; no OCEAN and no licence.
READINESS GATE, verified from the netlist of the run that EXECUTED
(psf/<test>/netlist/input.scs), not from the setup files. Two earlier MC attempts
on this cell failed it silently.
1. mismatchflag. DacNonlinTB and DacNonlinWPSUTB netlist 76 devices with
mismatchflag=1 and ZERO with mismatchflag=0; 74 of those are the ladder
(RS1/RS2/RP1..RP4 x 12 each, plus RTERM1/RTERM2). The four PSU-only benches
contain no ladder instance at all (0 matches for RS*/RP*/RTERM*) and carry 17
mismatchflag=1 devices each -- that is the PSU block, not a gap.
2. Model section. All six tests select section=castalia_pm_25, the section that
carries the statistics blocks. No test falls back to a tt_* list.
3. Tolerances. The two DAC tests run reltol=1e-6 vabstol=1e-9 iabstol=1e-15;
the four PSU tests run ADE defaults (reltol=1e-3 vabstol=1e-6 iabstol=1e-12).
Stated on the affected captions.
TEMPERATURE IS NOT UNIFORM. DacNonlinTB and DacNonlinWPSUTB are netlisted at
temp=25; LoadRegTB, LineRegTB, ZoutTB and PSUStartupTB at temp=27. Every caption
states the temperature of its own test. Do not total or compare sigmas across the
two groups without noting it.
EVERY SIGNAL NAME IS COPIED VERBATIM FROM THE RUN'S OWN mcparam. A name not in
mcparam is silently dropped from the table with only a log line. Note lsb, v_fs,
inl_lsb, dnl_min, voff_dac and gain_err exist in BOTH DAC tests with different
values -- they are kept in separate logical tests and never mixed in one table.
NO SENTINELS ANYWHERE. All six tests report N = 200/200 on every mcparam output;
no -1.11111e+36 and no NaN in any column. Nothing is held out of any statistic.
THE TWO DEFECTS ARE INDEPENDENT, and the corner run sees neither.
(a) The ladder is matching-limited and fails on an IDEAL rail: INL 1.490 +/-
0.625 LSB against 1 LSB (42/200), monotonic on 80/200, joint 34/200 = 17.0 %
of channels and 0.08 % of four-channel chips. lsb (sd 4.84e-10 V), v_fs
(sd 1.84e-6 V) and gain_err (sd 0.50 ppm) are effectively fixed, so all of
the linearity spread is resistor mismatch.
(b) The supply block modulates the reference: vddac_pp 25.835 mV against the
133 uV quarter-LSB budget (0/200), which turns the ratiometric -1.747 LSB
DNL into a raw -10.816 LSB and the INL into 36.78 LSB.
vddac_pp, raw dnl_min, load_reg, dvddac_load and zout_max are ONE defect
measured five ways, not five problems. Verified: load_reg vs zout_lf r = 0.966;
vddac_pp vs raw dnl_min r = -0.944; vddac_pp vs raw inl_lsb r = +0.903.
Ratiometric vs ideal-rail: inl r = 1.0000, dnl r = 1.0000.
SUPERSEDED CLAIM, must not reappear: an earlier prompt for this block asserted
'the ladder is excellent, only the supply is bad'. That came from a run whose
ladder had mismatchflag=0 and is FALSE.
THE 9.7 OHM FIGURE IS ALSO SUPERSEDED and is not printed anywhere. The
requirement is derived only from measured quantities: 133 uV / 25.835 mV = 1/193,
so the supply output impedance must fall by a factor of 193, to about 5 ohm,
against 894 ohm small-signal (zout_lf, the right one for the ladder's own ~23 uA
excursion about near-zero load) and 1133 ohm as a 0-100 uA chord (load_reg).
894/193 = 4.6, 1133/193 = 5.9. Quote the factor and ~5 ohm, never a false-precision
single number. No device dimensions or absolute resistance values appear in any
caption -- those are proprietary (see note_ampab_intro.tex); ratios only.
REFERENCE-CURRENT MODEL, transcribed from the netlist topology (RS1+RS2 = the
series R arm, RP1..RP4 = the 2R branch, RS2+RS1+RTERM looking left from the LSB
node = the 2R termination) and solved nodally with unit R: Out/Vref = code/4096 to
the last digit at every code, so the network ratio design is exact and contributes
no INL. I_ref = 0 at code 0, 0.2500 at 2048, 0.3333 at 4095, maximum 1.4444
Vref/R at code 1365 = 0b010101010101 -- which is where the measured vddac_min
lands on all 200 samples (sd exactly 0). The model maximum is degenerate: code
2731 = 0b101010101011 gives the identical 1.4444; not belaboured in the captions.
The fit VddDac = V0 - Rout*I_ref on the nominal tight-tolerance sweep gives
r = -0.9698, R^2 = 94.0 %, residual 931 uV rms against a 25.700 mV spread,
V0 = 2.1679 V. That fit is the coordinating agent's, from the nominal sweep
waveform; everything else in these captions is computed from mcdata here.
TABLE SPLIT. The brief asked for one PSU table (load_reg, dvddac_load, line_reg,
dvddac_line, i_q, zout_lf, zout_max). An mcstats table reads ONE test's mcparam,
and those rows live in three different tests, so it is emitted as three tables:
dacr2r12_mc_psu_load, dacr2r12_mc_psu_line, dacr2r12_mc_psu_zout. All three ids
must appear in the owning block's `order`.
DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS. Nothing is dropped silently.
PSUStartupTB -- the WHOLE TEST. The enable source is a pulse with delay=t_dly=1 s
and width=t_win=0 against a transient stop of t_end=500 us, so En never asserts
inside the simulated window. vddac_final is therefore 0.394 V (sd 40.8 mV): the
disabled state, not a settled startup value, against the 2.179 V the same block
reaches under DC in LoadRegTB. vddac_over (skew +3.95, 200/200 inside its 5 %
limit) and i_inrush (3.15 uA) grade a startup that did not happen, and t_startup
has no mcparam row at all. Publishing any of it would imply startup was
characterised. Fix the bench (t_dly << t_end) and re-run before publishing.
DacNonlinTB v_zs / voff_dac / vfs_dac -- bit-identical duplicates: voff_dac == v_zs
and vfs_dac == v_fs on all 200 samples. Published once, as v_fs and voff_lsb.
DacNonlinTB dnl_msb -- the DNL at the mid-scale transition. It is not an
independent quantity: |dnl_msb| equals dnl_lsb on 131 of 200 samples and
dnl_msb equals dnl_min on 83, i.e. the MSB transition IS the worst code about
two thirds of the time. Its own distribution is bimodal (mean -0.495, sd 2.452,
